messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: stat_contour on irregular dataset
parts:
Dear all,

Is this a bug or intend behaviour? When I try to use stat_contour on a irregular dataset, ggplot2 throw an error.

set.seed(12345)
tmp <- data.frame(POINT_X = runif(100), POINT_Y = runif(100), Estimate = runif(100))
#geom_point works
ggplot(tmp, aes(x = POINT_X, y = POINT_Y, colour = Estimate)) + geom_point()
#stat_contour does not work
ggplot(tmp, aes(x = POINT_X, y = POINT_Y, z = Estimate)) + stat_contour()

When I usie a gridded dataset everything works fine.

tmp <- expand.grid(POINT_X = runif(10), POINT_Y = runif(10))
tmp$Estimate <- runif(nrow(tmp))
ggplot(tmp, aes(x = POINT_X, y = POINT_Y, z = Estimate)) + stat_contour()
ggplot(tmp, aes(x = POINT_X, y = POINT_Y, colour = Estimate)) + geom_point()


Best regards,

Thierry

ir. Thierry Onkelinx
Instituut voor natuur- en bosonderzoek / Research Institute for Nature and Forest
team Biometrie & Kwaliteitszorg / team Biometrics & Quality Assurance
Kliniekstraat 25
1070 Anderlecht
Belgium

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: stat_contour on irregular dataset
parts:
hi,

ggplot2 internally sort the x and y and then call contourLines.
so unsorted data frame doesn't matter.

Probably, the problem is that your data frame (i.e., data matrix) is
too spase to estimate contour.
(but not sure because there is no document for the algorithms in contourLines.)
see ?contourLines

--

messages.subject: RE: stat_contour on irregular dataset
parts:
Dear Kohske and Brandon,

I've been playing a bit more and it seems to me that sparse data is not the problem.

#a nice grid and it works
set.seed(12345)
tmp <- expand.grid(POINT_X = 0:35, POINT_Y = 0:16)

tmp$Estimate <- runif(nrow(tmp))
ggplot(tmp, aes(x = POINT_X, y = POINT_Y, z = Estimate)) + stat_contour()

#adding a tiny bit of noise on the coordinates gives problems
tmp$POINT_X <- tmp$POINT_X + rnorm(nrow(tmp), sd = 0.0001)
tmp$POINT_Y <- tmp$POINT_Y + rnorm(nrow(tmp), sd = 0.0001)
ggplot(tmp, aes(x = POINT_X, y = POINT_Y, z = Estimate)) + stat_contour()
